sentences.text: Daemonosaurus was an extinct dinosaur from the Late Triassic period found in New Mexico, known only from a skull and neck fragments. It is characterized by a short, deep skull with large teeth and a rounded eye socket. Unlike other early dinosaurs which typically had four, Daemonosaurus had only three premaxillary teeth.
A large oval hole behind the rib articulations in the holotype specimen of Daemonosaurus has been equated with pneumatic pockets seen in other dinosaurs.
Daemonosaurus represents a lineage from the earliest dinosaur radiation that persisted alongside South American forms like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus until the end of the Triassic.
Fossil evidence suggests Daemonosaurus died after being washed into a pond and drowned during a sheet flood event.

Daemonosaurus was named by Sues, Nesbitt, Berman, and Henrici in 2011. The name Daemonosaurus means "demon reptile" derived from Greek words. The species name chauliodus means "prominent toothed" referring to its forward-pointing front teeth.

The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in a sediment block from the Coelophysis Quarry at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico. The fossil block containing the holotype was collected in the early 1980s by E.H. Colbert. The holotype specimen was first uncovered by a volunteer while the block was on loan to the State Museum of Pennsylvania.
Sues estimated Daemonosaurus to be around 1.5 meters long based on related theropod proportions. Holtz estimated Daemonosaurus was at most 2.2 meters long and weighed between 9.1 and 22.7 kilograms.
Daemonosaurus is classified as a basal theropod situated outside the Neotheropoda clade. The type species of the genus Daemonosaurus is Daemonosaurus chauliodus.

Phylogenetic analysis found Daemonosaurus chauliodus to be closely related to Tawa hallae. Daemonosaurus differs from Herrerasaurus by having much larger teeth in the premaxilla and distinct skull features. Daemonosaurus is distinguished from Eoraptor lunensis by possessing much larger premaxillary and anterior maxillary teeth. Daemonosaurus differs from Chindesaurus bryansmalli based on features of its cervical vertebrae.

Nesbitt and Sues (2020) considered Daemonosaurus a likely saurischian but could not conclusively place it within any specific dinosaur subgroup. Recent studies recovered Daemonosaurus in a clade named Morphoraptora alongside Tawa, Chindesaurus, and Ptychotherates. The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Daemonosaurus as Saurischia.

The only known specimen of Daemonosaurus was found at the Whitaker quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico. Daemonosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Rhaetian stage or possibly the latest Norian stage. Daemonosaurus lived between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
200 million years ago, the habitat of Daemonosaurus near the equator featured a warm, monsoon-like climate with heavy seasonal rain.
Daemonosaurus lived alongside early neotheropods like Coelophysis during the Late Triassic.
It is debated whether Daemonosaurus is a basal theropod or a non-theropod basal saurischian. A 2026 study proposed the clade Morphoraptora to group Daemonosaurus with Tawa and other herrerasaurians.
